title: peak_element_id comes from the 20-point truncated JSON, so it names an element from a different time step
mechanism: d3plot_reader._parse_series (line 564) quietly drops the '...(omitted N entries)...' marker: `data = [d for d in raw.get('data', []) if isinstance(d, dict)]`. Only the first 10 and last 10 states are left, and nothing records that the series is incomplete. PartTimeSeries.peak_element_id (models.py:108-117) first looks for an exact time match with time_of_max. If none exists, it silently falls back to `closest = min(self.data, key=lambda d: abs(d['time'] - self.time_of_max)); return closest.get('max_element_id')`. When the peak is in the omitted middle, this returns the max element of state 9 or of state n-10.
scenario: Committed sample python/koo_deep_report/single_report/analysis_result.json has 992 states. Part 1 has time_of_max=7.977e-05 and global_max=3748.5 MPa. Running _parse_series plus peak_element_id gives element 4218, which comes from t=9.09e-06, where the max is 0.43 MPa. Parts 2, 3 and 4 also get elements from t=9.09e-06, with maxima of 0.149, 0.234 and 0.034 MPa, against real peaks of 157, 261 and 65.5 MPa. Any run with more than 20 states and a peak outside the first or last 10 states is affected, which covers practically every drop test.
consumers: __main__._aggregate line 1332 `peak_element_id=st.peak_element_id` -> PartSummary -> html_report._build_js_data parts[pid].peak_element_id -> Deep Dive KPI card 'peak Element #N / max stress location' (html_report.py:1321-1323). Engineers use this element ID to locate the critical element.
suggested_fix: Have unified_analyzer write the element id at the global max (e.g. 'max_element_id_at_peak') next to global_max/time_of_max and read that. At minimum, return None when the exact time_of_max point is missing instead of substituting the nearest surviving point. Also keep a truncation flag on PartTimeSeries so consumers can tell the series is partial.

title: Shell and thick-shell parts appear with peak von Mises 0.00 MPa, and the 'solid only' label shows only when hotspot clustering ran
mechanism: The C++ stress_history comes only from the solid pass (UnifiedAnalyzer.cpp:195, 'Single-pass solid element analysis'). Motion covers every part. _aggregate builds all_part_ids from stress, strain and motion keys (__main__.py:1302-1306) and sets `peak_stress=st.global_max if st else 0.0` (line 1330), so a shell part becomes peak_stress=0.0. renderStress/renderOverview/updateDeepDive list every filteredParts() entry with `${fmt(p.peak_stress)} MPa`. The qualifier `const solidOnly = (DATA.hotspot || []).some(p => (p.element_type || 'solid') !== 'solid')` depends only on hotspot data, so without --hotspot-clusters the headline 'peak Von Mises stress' has no 'solid only' note.
scenario: A default koo_deep_report run (no --hotspot-clusters) on a phone drop deck where the PCB, FPCB or housing is shell-meshed. Each shell part appears in the 'Von Mises stress ranking' as '0.00 MPa' and the Deep Dive KPI shows 'peak stress 0.00 MPa (t=0.0000)'. The overview peak stress leaves out all shell parts and says nothing about it. result.json parts[pid].peak_stress is 0.0 for those parts.
consumers: report.html overview KPI, stress ranking bars, Deep Dive KPIs; result.json parts.peak_stress / safety_factor; batch_report part comparison (0 bars).
suggested_fix: Use None for parts that have no stress series and render them as '-' / 'not computed (shell)'. Derive the solid-only qualifier from the part element types in metadata (or from the absence of a stress series for parts that have motion), not from the hotspot list.

title: _downsample stride-decimates rcforc, motion, glstat, sleout and peak-tensor series to 500 points and loses spikes
mechanism: `step = (len(arr) - 1) / (n - 1); indices = {0, len(arr) - 1}; indices.update(int(i * step) for i in range(n)); return [arr[i] for i in sorted(indices)]` keeps evenly spaced samples and nothing else, with no min/max preservation. It is applied to motion (lines 232-239), glstat (276-282), rcforc fx/fy/fz/fmag (304-306), sleout (315-317) and peak_element_tensors (222-225). In the tensor tab the principal stresses, peakVmIdx ('Peak jump' button) and the tensor table are computed in JS from the decimated arrays, and `t.time.indexOf(t.peak_time)` fails when the peak sample was dropped.
scenario: Real data, /data/ball_drop_test_v3/ex07_hex8_m027_mortar/binout0000 (rcforc has 751 samples). For interface 2 'Rubber-Plate' the chart |F| peak is 206271 but the true peak_fmag is 231214 (-10.8%). Synthetic check: a 2001-sample acceleration series with a one-sample spike of 5000 at index 1001 gives chart max 1.0, because the kept indices around it are 997, 1002 and 1006. A 992-state d3plot (the committed sample) decimates motion and tensor histories.
consumers: report.html motion charts (disp/vel/acc), energy chart, contact force chart, sliding energy chart, stress tensor / ellipsoid / Mohr / table and the 'Peak jump' slider. The KPI peaks come from full data, so the charts contradict the tables.
suggested_fix: Use min/max-preserving decimation (per bucket, keep the argmin and argmax, or LTTB plus forced global extrema) with a shared index set per series group. For tensors, always splice in the peak_time index and compute peakVmIdx in Python from full data.

title: matsum chart: time axis is decimated but the [n_times][n_parts] energy rows are not, so energy is plotted at the wrong times
mechanism: `'t': _downsample(bn.matsum.t), 'internal_energy': [_downsample(e) for e in bn.matsum.internal_energy], 'kinetic_energy': [...]`. internal_energy has shape [n_times][n_parts] (binout_reader.py:14, lasso shape (751, 3)). _downsample(e) therefore acts on each time row across parts, and the time rows themselves are never decimated. In JS, updateMatsumChart does `ie = ms.internal_energy.map(row => row[idx])` (n_times values) and plots it against ms.t (500 values). Plotly keeps the shorter length, so row k is drawn at t_decimated[k]. When n_parts > 500, part columns are also decimated and idx no longer matches part_ids.
scenario: Real data, ex07_hex8_m027_mortar/binout0000: matsum has 751 times and 3 parts. The JS payload has t length 500 and internal_energy 751 rows. The last plotted x (t=0.015 s = t_end) shows the energy row for t=0.00998 s. Only the first two thirds of the simulation are drawn, stretched 1.5x over the full time axis, and the last third never appears.
consumers: report.html contact/energy tab, 'internal energy by material (matsum)' chart.
suggested_fix: Decimate along the time axis with one index set: `idx = indices(len(t)); t=[t[i] for i in idx]; ie=[internal_energy[i] for i in idx]` (or transpose to per-part series). Never apply _downsample to a row across parts.

title: JS fmt() uses fixed toFixed(2/4/5), so s-unit times, GPa stresses, small strains and contact impulses collapse to 0.00 or identical strings; unit labels are hard-coded MPa/mm
mechanism: `function fmt(v, dec=2) { ... if (Math.abs(v) >= 1e6) return v.toExponential(2); return Number(v).toFixed(dec); }`. It is used for stress KPIs `${fmt(s.peak_stress)} MPa` (683, 727, 776, 1310), strains `fmt(p.peak_strain,4)` (688, 788, 1311), times `fmt(p?.time_of_peak_stress,4)` (1310), `fmt(DATA.metadata.end_time,4)` (714, 2073), hotspot `fmt(c.peak_time, 5)` (2264), stress_max/stress_mean in the hotspot tables, and contact impulse `fx(i.impulse)` = fmt 2dp (1487). Line 1475 already notes that times collapse under fmt, but that is fixed only for the contact table. 'MPa' and 'mm' are literal strings regardless of the deck unit system.
scenario: node check: time_of_peak_stress 7.977e-05 s (the committed sample) -> '0.0001', and 1.2e-4 and 1.4e-4 both give '0.0001'. Hotspot peak_time 3.2e-6 -> '0.00000'. A kg-mm-ms deck with stress in GPa: 0.0863 -> '0.09 MPa', 0.0042 -> '0.00 MPa'. Strain 3e-5 or 4.9e-5 -> '0.0000'. Contact impulse 0.0042 N*s -> '0.00'.
consumers: report.html overview KPIs, stress/strain rankings, Deep Dive KPIs, tensor table, hotspot summary and detail tables, contact impulse column, system info time range.
suggested_fix: Format with significant digits, e.g. `Number(v).toPrecision(4)`, switching to exponent notation for |v| < 1e-3 (like hsMetricFmt or ft). Take the unit label from series.unit or metadata instead of the hard-coded 'MPa'/'mm'.

title: Batch table 'T end' uses toFixed(1), so every simulation in seconds shows 0.0; strain uses toFixed(4)
scenario: t_end=0.00100001 (committed sample result.json) -> '0.0'. Any drop test run in seconds (t_end 0.001-0.05) shows 0.0 or 0.1. Peak strain 4e-5 -> '0.0000', which reads as zero, whereas a true 0 renders as '-'.
consumers: batch_report.html case summary table and part comparison table.
suggested_fix: Use toPrecision or exponent formatting for t_end and strain (e.g. `Number(v).toPrecision(4)`).

title: Batch part comparison keys parts by name, so parts that share a name overwrite each other within a case
mechanism: `const pname = pdata.name || `Part ${pid}`; const key = pname; if (!ALL_PARTS[key]) ALL_PARTS[key] = { pid: parseInt(pid), cases: {} }; ALL_PARTS[key].cases[caseLabel] = pdata;`. Two PIDs with the same keyword title in one result.json map to the same key, and the later PID replaces the earlier one without any notice. CASE_LABELS/cases are also keyed by label, so two cases with the same label collide the same way.
scenario: A deck with PID 101 'SCREW' (peak 900 MPa) and PID 102 'SCREW' (peak 50 MPa). Object.entries iterates 101 then 102, so the 'SCREW' row shows 50 MPa, the 'max' column shows 50, and the 900 MPa part is gone from the table and chart. Repeated titles such as SCREW, FOAM or TAPE are common in assembly decks.
consumers: batch_report.html 'part comparison' tab table, max column and cross-case bar chart.
suggested_fix: Key by PID (or `${pid}|${name}`) and show the name as a label. Keep duplicate names as separate rows.

title: Batch output dir is output_root/<leaf dir name>, so sims with the same leaf name overwrite each other and one silently disappears
mechanism: `case_out = output_root / sim_info.path.name`. find_all uses `root.rglob('d3plot')` over the whole tree, so sims in A/Run_001 and B/Run_001, or X/output and Y/output, share case_out. run_analysis removes renders/ and rewrites analysis_result.json, result.json and report.html in the same folder, and with --threads>1 two workers write it at the same time. load_results_from_dir then finds one result.json per folder.
scenario: `koo_deep_report batch /data/campaigns` where Test_A/output/Run_001/d3plot and Test_B/output/Run_001/d3plot both exist. Both write to <out>/Run_001, and the batch report counts one case and shows only the last writer's numbers. Nothing lands in failed_cases.txt. With --skip-existing, the second sim is skipped because the first already produced result.json.
consumers: batch_report.html case counts, KPIs and tables; per-case report.html and result.json.
suggested_fix: Name case_out from the path relative to the batch root (e.g. 'Test_A__output__Run_001'), or detect duplicates and add a suffix, and warn.

title: has_mass_added is always False when glstat 'added mass' starts at 0, so mass-scaling warnings are suppressed
mechanism: `if len(self.mass) < 2 or self.mass[0] == 0: return False; return (self.mass[-1] - self.mass[0]) / self.mass[0] > 0.01`. GlstatData.mass holds the glstat 'added mass' line (glstat_reader._RE_MASS), not the model mass. Added mass is normally 0 at t=0, so the check returns False and the 'percentage increase' line is never read. When it does start nonzero, it measures growth of the added mass relative to itself, not relative to model mass.
scenario: Real glstat /data/shield_can_forming_study/ubend_c5210/glstat: added mass goes from 0.0 to 4.9451e-05 and 'percentage increase' is 2.37%, yet parse_glstat(...).has_mass_added is False. /data/alt_spg/ex02_sph_f1000/glstat: 0 -> 3.75e-07 with 'percentage increase' 1.73%, also False.
consumers: report.html energy tab massWarn box 'mass added detected' (html_report.py:1402).
suggested_fix: Parse 'percentage increase' (binout glstat 'percent_increase') and flag when it is > 1%, or compare added mass with the initial physical mass. Do not return False just because mass[0]==0.

title: The MAT field map reads the wrong card fields: yield from PR/HR/VP/C, FAIL from BETA/NUMINT
mechanism: _MAT_SIGY_MAP maps `15: (1, 4)`, `36: (1, 4)`, `98: (1, 4)`, `124: (1, 4)`, `18: (1, 4)` and _MAT_FAIL_MAP maps `3: (1, 6)`, `98: (1, 6)`. Actual card 1 layouts: MAT_015 is MID RO G E PR, so field 4 is PR. MAT_036 is MID RO E PR HR, so field 4 is HR. MAT_098 is MID RO E PR VP EPSO NUMINT, so fields 4 and 6 are VP and NUMINT. MAT_124 is MID RO E PR C P FAIL, so field 4 is C. MAT_003 is MID RO E PR SIGY ETAN BETA, so field 6 is BETA and FS sits on card 2. MAT_018 field 4 is K, the strength coefficient, not yield. get_design_criteria turns these into stress_limit/strain_limit with source 'mat_card'.
scenario: Parsing a test deck gives: *MAT_JOHNSON_COOK (PR=0.33, A=320) -> stress_limit 0.33 'mat_card'. *MAT_PLASTIC_KINEMATIC (BETA=1.0, FS=0.25) -> strain_limit 1.0 'mat_card'. *MAT_3-PARAMETER_BARLAT (HR=3) -> stress_limit 3.0. For a JC part at 300 MPa this yields safety_factor 0.0011, stress_ratio 909 and warning 'crit'.
consumers: __main__._aggregate -> PartSummary.safety_factor/stress_ratio/strain_ratio -> report.html SF badges in stress ranking and Deep Dive; result.json parts.*; console 'Design Criteria Warnings'; batch_report val-warn colouring.
suggested_fix: Fix the card/field table per the LS-DYNA manual (MAT_015 A is card 2 field 0; MAT_003 FS is card 2 field 2; MAT_098 A is card 2 field 0; MAT_124 SIGY is on card 2 or from the curve). For models without a scalar yield (018, 036, 124 with curves), leave stress_limit at 0 or 'none' instead of reading neighbouring fields.

title: Keyword parser drops every part after the first in a multi-part *PART block, all *PART_xxx variants and all *INCLUDE files; the impact loader then analyses only the surviving part IDs
mechanism: `if upper.startswith('*PART') and not upper.startswith('*PART_'): i = _parse_part(lines, i + 1, data)`. _parse_part reads one title plus one data card and returns `i + 1` (line 331), so further title/card pairs under the same *PART are skipped by the main loop because they do not start with '*'. *PART_CONTACT, *PART_INERTIA and *PART_COMPOSITE are excluded, and *INCLUDE is never followed. No warning is produced.
scenario: A *PART block with 'Housing / 10 1 5', 'Screen Glass / 11 1 5', 'Battery / 12 1 5' parses to {10: 'Housing'} only, so parts 11 and 12 have no name and no design criteria (safety_factor None). In koo_impact_report/loader.py (around line 1546), `part_ids_to_extract = sorted(kw_data.parts.keys())` is passed to run_analysis. unified_analyzer then runs only for the parsed IDs, and every part defined in the multi-part block, *PART_CONTACT or an *INCLUDE file is left out of the impact motion and stress analysis entirely.
consumers: koo_deep_report part names and design criteria (report.html, result.json); contact_metrics/energy_flow part names; koo_impact_report part selection for unified_analyzer (missing parts in impact report).
suggested_fix: Loop over title/card pairs until the next '*' line, parse *PART_* variants (skipping their extra cards), follow *INCLUDE relative to the deck. In the impact loader, do not narrow the part list to the keyword parse result, or verify it against the d3plot part list.

title: 'Peak displacement' is the max of the part-average displacement; the available Max_Disp_Mag column is ignored
mechanism: `def peak_disp_mag(self): return max(self.disp_mag)` where disp_mag is CSV 'Avg_Disp_Mag' (d3plot_reader.py:606). `peak_max_disp` (max of 'Max_Disp_Mag') exists but is never used. _aggregate sets `peak_disp_mag=mo.peak_disp_mag` (__main__.py:1339) and `peak_disp_global = max(p.peak_disp_mag ...)` (1376).
scenario: A cantilevered PCB flexing under a drop: nodes at the tip move 20 mm while the part average is 5 mm. The report shows 'peak displacement 5.00 mm' in the overview KPI, the motion tab 'max displacement ranking' and batch 'peak displacement (mm)', which understates the real max nodal displacement 4x. The committed sample shows part 1 peak_disp_mag 5.14 mm.
consumers: report.html overview KPI, motion 'max displacement ranking' bars, Deep Dive KPI; result.json summary.peak_disp_global and parts.peak_disp_mag; batch_report table and part comparison.
suggested_fix: Report max(Max_Disp_Mag) as 'peak displacement' (with its node id), and label the average-based value explicitly as 'peak average displacement' if it is kept.

title: Energy-flow edges: engage index defaults to 0 when a short pulse falls between decimated samples, and impulse/force are rounded to 4 decimals
mechanism: force_mag_ts is point-sampled at the decimated ref_t (`_resample(rt, fm, ref_t)`, step ceil(n/max_pts); only the global total-force argmax is spliced in). `first_engage_idx = 0; for k, f in enumerate(force_mag_ts): if f > thr: first_engage_idx = k; break`, so if no sample exceeds thr the index stays 0, i.e. 'engaged at t0'. energy_flow_csv.py:74 writes `t_engage = times[fe_idx]`. `_r4` is `round(xf, 4)` (and inf/nan -> 0.0) for peak_force, total_impulse, total_work, kinetic_ts and internal_ts.
scenario: Synthetic run through build_flow_graph (2000 matsum samples at 5 us, max_pts=200 as in energy_flow_csv): a secondary interface with a 50 N pulse over indices 1001-1003 (t=5.005 ms). Result: max(force_mag_ts)=0.0, first_engage_idx=0, CSV t_engage=0.0 instead of 0.005005, and total_impulse=0.0007 (true 7.5e-4). A 0.9 N x 40 us contact gives total_impulse 3.15e-5 N*s, rounded to 0.0 even though the edge is kept as engaged. Real ex07 binout: t_engage for CID 1 is 7.97e-5 against a true engage_t0 of 5.99e-5 (decimation step 4).
consumers: energy_flow_edges.csv (t_engage, total_impulse, peak_force, total_work) in every koo_deep_report output with binout; koo_impact_report and koo_sphere_report energy-flow panels (force heatmap from decimated e.f, Sankey impulse widths).
suggested_fix: Compute first_engage time on the full-resolution rt/fm (as contact_metrics does), store the time itself, and use None when nothing crosses thr. Resample with bucket max instead of point samples. Round with significant digits (e.g. float(f'{x:.6g}')) instead of 4 decimal places.
